title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 67
paragraphs: Lichas, being one of these, discovered it in Tegea by means both of luck and skill. For at that time there were dealings under a truce with the men of Tegea, and he had come to a forge there and was watching iron being worked, and he stood marveling at what was being done. The smith, perceiving that he was astonished, ceased from his work and said: “Surely, stranger of Lacedaemon, if you had seen what I once saw, you would have marveled much more—since now it happens that you marvel so greatly at the working of this iron. For I, wishing to dig a well in this enclosure, in my digging came upon a coffin seven cubits long; and not believing that there had ever been men larger than those of the present day, I opened it, and I saw that the dead body was equal in length to the coffin. Then, after I had measured it, I filled in the earth over it again.” So the smith told him what he had seen; and the other, reflecting on what he had been told, conjectured that this was Orestes according to the saying of the Oracle, forming his conjecture in the following way: seeing that the smith had two pairs of bellows, he concluded that these were the “blasts” spoken of, and that the anvil and the hammer were the stroke and the counter-stroke, and that the iron which was being worked was the “trouble laid upon trouble,” reasoning that iron has been discovered for the harm of mankind. Having thus conjectured, he returned to Sparta and declared the whole matter to the Lacedaemonians. They, however, brought a charge against him on a fictitious pretext and drove him out into exile. So having come to Tegea, he told the smith of his misfortune and tried to rent the enclosure from him. At first the smith would not allow him to have it, but at last Lichas persuaded him and took up his abode there. Then he dug up the grave, gathered together the bones, and went away with them to Sparta. From that time on, whenever they made trial of one another, the Lacedaemonians had much the advantage in war, and by now they had subdued to themselves the greater part of the Peloponnesus besides.
